subject: Enablement roadmap: environment prerequisites & ownership grid
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha@gridlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Enablement roadmap: environment prerequisites & ownership grid

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed enablement roadmap for the POC environment so we can align owners and target a short pilot window:

High-level POC target: 2-week functional trial with production-like traffic profile; target close (pilot kickoff): 2026-10-29.

Key environment prerequisites (we discussed these live):
- VPC peering & route table updates (required for model control plane -> customer VPC egress)
- IP allowlist for Redwood egress and health-check IPs
- SSO/SAML integration for test users (IdP metadata + assertion attributes)
- Secrets & KMS access (short-lived dev keys + optional customer-managed KMS)

Proposed milestone slate (ownership grid in attached workbook):
1) Network readiness (VPC peering scheduled + BGP/route tests) — owner: GridLytics networking (ops-team@gridlytics.com) / Redwood infra lead: ben_carter
2) IP allowlist applied & port validations — owner: GridLytics security / Redwood SE: ben_carter
3) SSO/SAML test config (test SP, assertion mapping) — owner: GridLytics IdP admin (Aisha) / Redwood integration: laura_bennett
4) Secrets & KMS (access pattern + test service account) — owner: GridLytics cloud infra / Redwood ops: marissa_cole
5) Smoke tests & baseline perf (dry run + tokenization/latency checks) — owner: Redwood SE + GridLytics devs

Dependencies we flagged:
- Customer needs to open peering request and share VPC IDs and route tables by 2026-10-08.
- SSO metadata + test accounts required by 2026-10-12.
- KMS policy review for customer-managed keys by 2026-10-15 (optional; we can use short-lived Redwood-managed keys if needed).

Next steps I propose this week:
- Aisha: confirm VPC ID, CIDR, and preferred peering window (pick 2 potential windows).
- Ops-team: confirm IP allowlist process and length of maintenance window needed for route updates.
- Laura: I'll loop you in to capture SAML attribute mapping and provide a template.
- Ben/Marissa: draft a short-runbook for post-peering smoke tests so GridLytics SMEs can validate.

I attached a one-sheet enablement workbook (tab: ownership-grid) and the network diagram we sketched in the call.

If that looks right, I'll convert the workbook to the Mutual Action Plan canonical format and share an editable link.

Thanks —
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment stubs: enablement_playbook_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), gridlytics-network-diagram.png (image)

From: Aisha Malik <aisha@gridlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: GridLytics Ops <ops-team@gridlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enablement roadmap: environment prerequisites & ownership grid

Thanks Karthik — this is very clear and helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) VPC peering: We can open the request today. VPC IDs below: vpc-0a1b2c3d (prod-sim), vpc-0d3c2b1a (dev-sim). Preferred windows: 2026-10-12 02:00-04:00 UTC or 2026-10-14 22:00-00:00 UTC. Which works better on your side?

2) IP allowlist: Our security team prefers a short maintenance window and CIDR ranges; can you provide the minimal egress IPs Redwood requires?

3) SSO/SAML: We will provide IdP metadata and 5 test users by 2026-10-12. One note: our SAML assertions include an "employeeType" attribute — does Redwood need a specific attribute name for role mapping?

4) KMS: We prefer customer-managed keys but are open to a hybrid approach for the POC. Please outline the minimum IAM roles or KMS bindings you need for the short-lived test keys.

I'll loop in our cloud infra lead (ops-team) to confirm the peering windows.

-Aisha

Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enablement roadmap: environment prerequisites & ownership grid

Aisha — great, thanks for the details. Responding inline below plus an updated ownership grid (tab: owners_v1) in the workbook.

1) VPC peering windows: Redwood prefers the 2026-10-14 22:00-00:00 UTC window (lower traffic on our side). Ben, can you reserve an infra slot for the peering and route validation then?

2) Egress IPs / allowlist: minimal egress is three static IPs for control-plane health checks and provisioning: 34.213.45.90, 34.213.45.91, 34.213.45.92. We'll also provide a fallback /24 on request for larger customers. Security note: health-checks originate from control-plane and from worker nodes (covered by the minimal set).

3) SAML attributes: Redwood can map to "employeeType" — our default mapping is to either "role" or "employeeType"; Laura will confirm the exact attribute name we use in the test SP. We handle nameID/email + custom attributes for role mapping.

4) KMS bindings: For the POC we need a service account with: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the test key and iam.serviceAccountUser for the Redwood service account. If you prefer Redwood-managed keys, we'll use short-lived tokens with strict TTLs.

Milestone ownership (short form):
- Network & peering: GridLytics Ops / ben_carter (Redwood)
- IP allowlist: GridLytics Security / ben_carter
- SSO/SAML: GridLytics IdP / laura_bennett (Redwood)
- Secrets/KMS: GridLytics Cloud Infra / marissa_cole (Redwood)

I'll convert this to a canonical MAP once we lock the dates. If everyone agrees, I'll schedule the peering on 2026-10-14 and send a calendar invite for a 1-hour window for initial route tests (ben to lead).

Thanks —
Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Karthik / team — I'm good to lead the peering slot on 2026-10-14 22:00-00:00 UTC. Quick notes for the runbook I'm preparing (will attach a short checklist):
- Pre-change: confirm VPC ID and route table snapshots (GridLytics to provide)
- During window: create peering, update routes, validate asymmetric routes, run traceroutes to control-plane endpoints
- Post-change: run tokenization/latency smoke tests (samples provided by Marissa)

IP allowlist: we'll provide a one-line CIDR fallback if ops needs it, but please try minimal three IPs above first. Also confirm if your firewall requires ports TCP 443 and UDP 123 for NTP sync checks.

I'm drafting the runbook and test scripts today and will drop them into the shared Drive link (see related_links).

Ben
